assistantMessageEvent.content:
The user asks a SQLite-specific question about WAL sidecars during a file-copy restore of a live DB. Answer concisely, three lines max.

Facts: In WAL mode, committed transactions may live in the -wal file and not yet be checkpointed into the main DB. If you copy only brain.sqlite over a live database, you get a stale/mismatched main DB while the old -wal/-shm remain, containing pages from the *other* database lineage; SQLite validates the WAL header salt/checksum against... actually SQLite will attempt recovery from the -wal and can apply frames that don't belong to the new DB file, producing corruption or "database disk image is malformed". Also the -shm is shared memory index; stale -shm with a replaced main file → mismatched wal-index, possible SQLITE_CORRUPT or lost/uncommitted data.

Correct procedure: stop all connections (or use SQLite backup API / `VACUUM INTO`), checkpoint (TRUNCATE) then copy all three files atomically, or better delete -wal/-shm before/after restore so SQLite recreates them. Standard guidance: copy the main DB plus sidecars, or ensure no live connections and remove -wal/-shm.

Also note: three-line limit. Prioritize the failure mode: stale WAL frames applied to the new main DB → corruption; and uncommitted-but-committed data in the live -wal is discarded → data loss/rollback of acknowledged transactions.

Give the answer. Keep to ≤3 lines. Mention atomicity: copy all three while no connections, or delete sidecars.

Three lines:

1. Stop all connections first; a WAL-mode DB's committed data can live in `-wal`, so copy `brain.sqlite` with its `-wal`/`-shm` together, or delete both sidecars so SQLite recreates them (safer: checkpoint TRUNCATE or `VACUUM INTO`).
2. Skipping it leaves a stale WAL whose frames reference pages of the old database lineage; SQLite replays them onto the new main file → `SQLITE_CORRUPT` / "database disk image is malformed", or silent loss of transactions the replaced WAL had acknowledged.
3. Restore is also not atomic across three files: a crash mid-copy mixes generations; do it offline (or via the online Backup API) — never file-copy over a live DB.

1. Stop every connection (WAL-mode commits can live only in `-wal`), then either copy `brain.sqlite` together with `-wal`/`-shm` in one atomic step, or drop both sidecars so SQLite recreates them — safest is a checkpoint (`TRUNCATE`) or `VACUUM INTO` before the swap.
2. Skipping it leaves a stale `-wal` whose frames belong to the *old* file's lineage; SQLite replays them over the new main file → `SQLITE_CORRUPT` / "database disk image is malformed", or silent loss/rollback of transactions the discarded WAL had already acknowledged (`-shm` mismatch alone usually just forces a WAL restart).
3. This is also a torn three-file update: a crash mid-copy mixes generations, so do the restore offline or via the Online Backup API — never a plain file copy over a live DB.
